newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony, others develop new IC memory card format.
newsitem.headline: Sony, others develop new IC memory card format.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Wednesday that it and other major electronics firms have jointly developed a new integrated circuit (IC) memory card format suitable for use in recording and playback of sound and still picture images.
The other firms involved in the development are Casio Computer Co Ltd, Sanyo Electric Co Ltd, Sharp Corp, Fujitsu Ltd and Olympus Optical Co Ltd, Sony said in a statement.

The card can be used in products such as digital still cameras. It has a recording capacity ranging from two to 32 megabytes, and can record in eight kilobyte block sizes compared to conventional recording in 512 bytes, Sony said.
The small size of the card would enable manufacturers to design smaller products, it said in a statement.
The new format is compatible between audiovisual hardware produced by different manufacturers, it said.
